On October 14, 2026, the Company issued a press release titled “Entrada Therapeutics Announces Positive Results from the First Cohort of Participants with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) in the Phase 1/2 ELEVATE-45-201 Study of ENTR-601-45.” A copy of the press release is furnished hereto as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated herein by reference. The information in Item 7.01 of this Current Report on Form 8-K, including the accompanying Exhibit 99.1, is intended to be furnished and shall not be deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act or otherwise subject to the liability of such section, nor shall it be deemed incorporated by reference in any filing under the Securities Act or the Exchange Act, except as expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing. Item 8.01 Other Events. Update on ENTR-601-45 On October 14, 2026, the Company announced positive topline data from Cohort 1 of the double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending dose (MAD) portion of the Phase 1/2 ELEVATE-45-201 clinical study of ENTR-601-45 in ambulatory participants with a confirmed mutation in the DMD gene amenable to exon 45 skipping. ELEVATE-45-201 is a global, two-part, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1/2 study evaluating the safety, tolerability and effectiveness of ENTR-601-45 in ambulatory participants aged four to 20 with Duchenne who are amenable to exon 45 skipping. The multiple ascending dose (MAD) Part A portion of the study is evaluating the safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and functional parameters following intravenous administration of ENTR-601-45 to study participants in three cohorts at sites in the U.K. and EU. Cohort 1 of the MAD portion of the study enrolled eight participants with Duchenne. They were randomized 3:1 to receive ENTR-601-45 at a dose of 5 mg/kg or placebo, administered intravenously. During this double-blind period, doses were administered on days one, 43 and 85, and muscle biopsies were performed at the time of screening and at six weeks after the last dose. Following the initial three doses administered in Part A, all participants continued into the Phase 2, open-label portion in which the safety and efficacy of ENTR-601-45 are evaluated over a longer period of time. Cohort 2 enrollment is complete and dosing at 10 mg/kg is ongoing. The Company is on track to report data from Cohort 2 (10 mg/kg) in the first half of 2027, with data from Cohort 3 (up to 15 mg/kg) to follow. Highlights from the topline results of Cohort 1 of ELEVATE-45-201 include: Dystrophin measured by western blot and normalized to MHC; Dystrophin values are actual observed values, including values <LLOQ; Two participants in the ENTR-601-45 group had baseline dystrophin levels <LLOQ and >LOD; LLOQ for dystrophin was 0.25%; LOD for dystrophin was 0.1%; Biopsy performed at baseline; LLOQ: Lower limit of quantification; LOD: Limit of detection; MHC: Myosin heavy chain. Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics • Favorable safety and tolerability with ENTR-601-45 at the 5 mg/kg dose o Headache (5 events in 2 participants) was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) o One participant experienced 2 serious TEAEs (vomiting and pyrexia) which subsequently resolved o There were no study discontinuations due to any cause, and all participants enrolled in the open-label extension • No hypomagnesemia or renal safety concerns were noted o Renal markers, including eGFR and cystatin C, were within normal ranges in treated participants o Magnesium levels were also within the normal range • Plasma ENTR-601-45 exposures were consistent with those predicted by juvenile non-human primate (NHP) data o Modeled plasma exposures provide confidence in a significant increase in dystrophin expression at higher doses in Cohort 2 (10 mg/kg) and Cohort 3 (up to 15 mg/kg) Dystrophin Production, Exon Skipping and Functional Benefit • A mean increase of 0.10% (n = 6, nominal p = 0.03) from baseline in dystrophin production was observed in study participants who received ENTR-601-45 versus a 0.02% mean decrease from baseline in study participants who received placebo • A mean increase of 0.15% (n = 5, no p-value calculated) from baseline in exon skipping was observed in study participants who received ENTR-601-45 versus a 0.04% mean decrease from baseline in study participants who received placebo • Based on the age of Cohort 1 participants and baseline levels of function, no observable functional benefit was expected or observed after three doses of ENTR-601-45 • Functional impact will be assessed with higher doses and over longer dosing periods via future cohorts and the open-label studies Forward-Looking Statements This Current Report on Form 8-K contains express and implied forward-looking statements that involve substantial risks and uncertainties.
